title: Breaking redundancy of plant transporters: synthetic amiRNAs empower genetics
content: Transporter proteins are found in every cell type and are involved in moving a wide range of substrates, including amino acids, mineral ions, hormones, and other metabolites (Mishra et al. 2024). In plants, many transporters are encoded by large multi-gene families. Within these families there is variation in cell-type expression patterns as well as substrate specificity and affinity. These large families with partially overlapping function can make the use of conventional forward genetic screening challenging, as single mutants often show no phenotypic abnormalities (Rouached et al. 2008).
